title: Discord TagDuel lobby-cancel and private-concession interaction flow
scenarios: Build the real public tagPublicMessage lobby panel, extract its emitted cancel custom_id, pass it through the real handleTagComponent, assert deferUpdate occurs while the lobby is still active, then assert cancelled public payload and refresh.

Build the real private tagPrivateMessage, extract the emitted quit custom_id, pass it through handleTagComponent, verify the first click only opens confirmation, extract the emitted confirm custom_id, and pass it through the real handler. Assert acknowledgement precedes concession, the opposite team wins, the finished private panel has no live actions, and the public refresh observes finished state.
invariants: Real Discord.js builders and the real TagDuel interaction handler are exercised offline.
The cancel and confirm custom_ids are read from emitted payloads rather than hard-coded guesses.
The handler defers interaction updates before mutating persistent TagDuel state.
The private concession sequence is two-step and cannot finish the duel on the initial quit click.
The handler refreshes the public duel after a committed concession.
No live Discord token or network session is used.
limits: Fake Discord interaction objects exercise real builders/handler but do not call Discord API.
The tests cover lobby cancellation and team concession, not every component or modal.
No runtime, resolver, catalog manifest, allowlist, persistent database or player data is modified.
This is a Discord transport regression and certifies no new card behavior.
command: npm run check && npm run build && node --test tests/tagDiscordLobbyAndConcessionFlow2v2.test.cjs
